ideas.ablation_behavior_off: alpha_i set to 1 and u_i set to the zero vector for every item, leaving the curved chain, the transport and lambda exactly as in the full run.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the single trained run, with alpha_i and u_i from training transitions and the c=1 curved chain both active.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c treated as 0 for the chain: p advances by plain vector addition, Pi is the identity, lambda = 1, so the quantizer is the usual Euclidean residual chain with the behaviour gain retained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training-split sequential interactions only: S_i = multiset of next items observed after item i inside training sessions, capped at the 32 highest-count successors; N_i = 32 items drawn with probability proportional to training popularity from the same popularity decile as S_i, excluding i, its 1-hop neighbours and its successors, with a seed keyed deterministically on the item id. Then u_i = mean_{j in S_i} log_{x_i}(x_j) - mean_{j in N_i} log_{x_i}(x_j), all log maps in the ball of curvature 1, and the gain is a dimensionless ratio of hyperbolic norms (so it survives any uniform radial rescaling of the chart).
ideas.behavior_signal: Per-item directed successor contrast against a popularity-matched null, computed in the hyperbolic tangent space at the item's own point.
ideas.cost_estimate: No extra epochs. One preprocessing pass: 24556 items x (32 successor draws + 32 null draws), two log maps each, O(n*d) memory (about 12-25 MB at d=64-128); minutes once, off the training clock. Per optimisation step at the frozen scale (global batch 4096, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs): L x K x 4096 closed-form ball distances (L=3, K=256 gives 3.1M), each O(d) plus one scalar conformal factor and one rank-1 transport correction; roughly 2-3x the baseline nearest-neighbour quantizer cost, which is a minor fraction of a step because the text/ID encoder dominates. Expected Stage2 wall-clock overhead 3-6 percent, Stage3 cost unchanged.
ideas.coupling_equation: J_l(k) = lambda(p_l)^{-2} * [ alpha_i * <r_l - Pi(e_{l,k}), Pi(u_i)>^2 + || (r_l - Pi(e_{l,k}))_perp ||^2 ], k* = argmin_k J_l(k), with r_l = log_{p_l}(x_i), Pi = Pi_{0->p_l}, lambda(p) = 2/(1-c||p||^2), c = 1.
ideas.coupling_path: behaviour direction u_i and gain alpha_i -> transported residual decomposition in the level-l objective -> argmin over codewords -> prefix p_{l+1} through exp_p -> next level's transport and conformal factor -> SID tokens. Removing behaviour makes the form isotropic (argmin returns the plain nearest codeword of the curved chain); removing the curve makes the chain additive Euclidean with lambda=1; either change alters the chosen tokens.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the contrast direction computed from training transitions marks variation the generator can actually predict, then absorbing that direction earlier in the chain makes prefix-conditioned next-token prediction easier, and Stage3 test_recall@10 rises above 0.065 while the code-space within-successor / within-null distance ratio falls. Observed by per-level token-flip rate against the baseline SIDs (small at level 0, large at levels 1-2), the code-space contrast ratio, hyperbolic residual norms per level, and finally test_recall@10 from the single frozen Stage3 run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the quantizer, at codeword selection and at prefix accumulation, and in the gradient that reaches the encoder and the codebooks; not in the decoder's reconstruction loss and not in any standalone regularizer.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincaré ball of fixed curvature c=1, gauge-fixed by the data-derived radial scale s = 0.9/max||z||; operations are exp_0, log_p, exp_p, parallel transport Pi_{0->p}, and the conformal factor lambda(p) = 2/(1-c||p||^2) that defines the curved norm of a tangent residual.
ideas.key_change: Each level's codeword is chosen by minimizing a curved, contrast-weighted quadratic form of the transported residual (gain alpha_i along the behaviour direction u_i, uniform orthogonal), and the prefix point advances by an exponential map instead of a vector addition.
ideas.leakage_boundary: u_i and alpha_i are computed once before Stage2 from training interactions and the frozen training item text embeddings, stored as constants, never recomputed from validation or test interactions; the null sampler sees only training popularity; Stage3 never feeds back into SID construction; no item outside the 24556 training item set contributes to any SID.
ideas.motivation: In RQ-VAE the SID is a residual chain: level-0 explains most of the item, and the later tokens only explain what level-0 left over. For a generative next-item recommender the later tokens must be predictable from the prefix, i.e. they should carry behaviour-predictable variation, not encoder noise. The measured evidence here says what predicts Recall@10 is a behaviour-contrast quantity (successor-vs-null distance contrast), not hierarchy and not curvature; here that contrast is made the thing the residual chain spends code on, inside a curved metric where the same tangent residual moves the codeword point by a state-dependent amount.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds put behaviour into the codebook update (successor-weighted Fréchet means), into per-level curvature (CURVCTRL, which the gauge evidence undermines), into radial ranking (BRad-RQ) or into prefix/subtree boosting. This idea never sets curvature from data, never uses a Fréchet mean, and never uses a radius rank: curvature is a declared gauge (c=1), and behaviour enters as an anisotropic direction plus a gain INSIDE the residual-chain assignment rule, multiplied by the conformal factor of the ball. The coupling lives in the quantizer's argmin and in the exponential-map composition, not in an auxiliary loss beside the quantizer.
ideas.observables: per-level SID token flip rate against the baseline SID; code-space contrast ratio = mean d_P(prefix pair inside a successor set) / mean d_P(prefix pair to the null set); per-level hyperbolic residual norm; Stage3 test_recall@10.
risks: The contrast direction may be dominated by popularity even after null matching, drifting codes toward popular items; the curved chain may saturate near the boundary and raise reconstruction error; greedy per-level curves only bite from level 1 (level 0 sits at the origin); and better code-space contrast may not become token-level predictability, which is exactly what the one run must reveal.
ideas.safeguards: clamp ||p|| to 0.995 inside every exp_p and log_p denominator; clamp the artanh argument to 1-1e-7; if ||u_i||_{x_i} < 1e-6 or |S_i| < 2, set alpha_i = 1 and u_hat_i = 0 (that item silently falls back to isotropic); transport preserves the tangent norm up to lambda(0)/lambda(p), so rescale the residual by lambda(p) before the commitment term to keep the frozen beta meaningful; alpha is clipped to [0.5, 2.0] by a budget argument (no item may claim more than twice the median residual budget), not by search; the radial gauge s comes from max||z|| and c is never fitted, so no curvature estimate is claimed.
ideas.spec_equations: exp_0(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)/(sqrt(c)||v||) * v; for the Mobius form use w = ((1-c||p||^2)v - (1-c||v||^2)p)/(1 - 2c<p,v> + c^2||p||^2||v||^2), log_p(v) = (2/(c(1-c||p||^2))) * artanh(sqrt(c)||w||)/(sqrt(c)||w||) * w; exp_p(r) = p (+) tanh(sqrt(c)||r||)/(sqrt(c)||r||) r; Pi_{0->p}(v) = (lambda(0)/lambda(p)) * (v - c<p,v>/(1+sqrt(1-c||p||^2)) p); lambda(p) = 2/(1-c||p||^2); ||v||_p = lambda(p)||v||; u_hat_i = u_i/||u_i||_{x_i}; alpha_i = clip(||u_i||_{x_i} / median_j ||u_j||_{x_j}, 0.5, 2.0). Quantize: p_0 = 0; for l in 0..L-1: r_l = log_{p_l}(x_i); for each k: g_{l,k} = Pi_{0->p_l}(e_{l,k}), a = <r_l - g_{l,k}, Pi_{0->p_l}(u_hat_i)>, b = ||r_l - g_{l,k}||^2 - a^2, J = lambda(p_l)^{-2}(alpha_i a^2 + b); k* = argmin J; token_l = k*; p_{l+1} = exp_{p_l}(r_l - g_{l,k*}). Loss = sum_l lambda(p_l)^{-2}(alpha_i a_l^2 + b_l) + beta*||sg[e] - r||^2 with the frozen baseline beta, decoder term unchanged.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: frozen item text embeddings z (24556 x d), training transition counts, codebooks e (L x K x d), gain alpha (24556,), direction u_hat (24556 x d). Outputs: SID tokens (24556 x L), updated encoder parameters, updated codebooks, per-level prefix points, and the recorded diagnostics.

specification.text: Map frozen item text embedding z_i to x_i = exp_0(s z_i) with c=1, s = 0.9/max_i||z_i||. Precompute once, from the training split only, alpha_i and unit u_i (see BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION). Quantize x_i by the greedy curved chain of SPEC EQUATIONS. Train the encoder and the codebooks with that same per-level objective plus the standard commitment term; the codebooks receive the gradient of the curved objective, so their positions are shaped by the curved metric rather than by a Euclidean mean.

ideas.title: Curved residual chain with a behaviour-contrast anisotropic metric: the RQ-VAE quantizes in a Poincaré ball so that the training-only successor-vs-matched-null contrast direction absorbs code capacity before the deeper tokens do

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: flag BEHAV=0 sets u_hat_i = 0 for every item, hence p_i = o, r_1 = a_i and PT_{o->o} = identity, so the code is the plain Lorentz RQ on the content latent and codes are chosen without any item-specific frame; wired as a single branch on the pole table, never trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the single trained configuration: BEHAV=1 and GEOM=1, i.e. p_i = exp_o(u_hat_i), residuals by Lorentz log at a moving base point, codes transported by PT before the argmin, one 3000-epoch four-GPU Stage 2 run then the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping, no extra seeds, no sweep of any constant.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: flag GEOM=0 keeps the same pole but replaces every Lorentz map with its Euclidean counterpart (p_i stored as the tangent vector u_hat_i, z_0 = u_hat_i, z_l = z_{l-1} + c_{l,k}, r_l = x_i - z_{l-1}, no transport), so the behaviour enters only as a translation and the curvature-induced rotation is gone; wired as a branch that swaps the operator table, never trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training interactions only, within sessions, count ordered pairs (i -> j) giving n_ij, outgoing counts n_i, incoming counts n_j, total transitions N. Compute A_ij = max(0, log(N*n_ij/(n_i*n_j))) clipped at log N (the analytic maximum, since n_ij <= min(n_i,n_j)). Project successor content directions t_j (the frozen text/metadata embeddings already used by the RQ-VAE input, dimension d) with these weights, subtract the background term (sum_j A_ij) * t_pop where t_pop = sum_j (n_j/sum n) t_j, and L2-normalise. Items with no outgoing train transition get u_i = 0 and are routed to the identity frame.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed sequential co-consumption contrast: for every training item, the popularity-adjusted (PMI) successor direction from its outgoing session transitions, centred on the popularity-background content direction.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per step at the frozen scale (batch 4096, L=4, d=64): 9 closed-form Lorentz maps per item (5 log/exp for the residual-and-compose recursion, 4 transports, each O(d), no matrices) = about 18 kflops per item, about 74 MFLOP forward and about 0.2 GFLOP forward+backward per step; 24 steps per epoch gives about 5 GFLOP per epoch and about 16 TFLOP over 3000 epochs, i.e. well under 1 percent of a 4-GPU transformer step. One-off offline preprocessing: one pass over the training interactions to build n_ij, n_i, n_j (minutes on CPU), one N-by-d pole table (24556 by 64 float32 = 6.3 MB) held as a non-trainable buffer and gathered by item id, so no per-step graph and no extra parameter. Expected wall clock within 1 percent of the baseline 3000-epoch Stage 2 run.
ideas.coupling_equation: r_1(i) = log^c_{p_i}(x_i) with p_i = exp^c_o(u_hat_i) and u_hat_i = unit( sum_j max(0, PMI_ij) t_j - (sum_j max(0, PMI_ij)) t_pop ); assignment k_1(i) = argmin_k || r_1(i) - PT^c_{o->p_i}(c_{1,k}) ||^2. The behaviour term is u_hat_i (through p_i), the curved terms are exp^c_o, log^c_{p_i} and PT^c; neither can be dropped without changing r_1 and the argmin.
ideas.coupling_path: successor PMI contrast -> pole direction u_hat_i -> base point p_i on the hyperboloid -> residual r_1 = log_{p_i}(x_i) and transported codes PT_{o->z_{l-1}}(c) -> argmin code choice -> codebook/commitment gradients -> SID prefix tokens -> Stage 3 next-token prediction. Removing the behaviour (p_i = o) collapses the frame to the origin and removes all item-specific rotation; removing the geometry (Euclidean shift by u_hat_i, plain addition) keeps the behaviour shift but removes the gyration, so the assignment changes.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Worth keeping only if (a) the item-specific transport rotation is large enough to move code assignment (the mean gyration angle of PT_{o->p_i} on the orthogonal complement is of order the geodesic distance, i.e. O(1) rad at radius 1, recorded once at initialisation, and the level-1 code histogram differs from the Euclidean-shift variant by a large fraction of items), and (b) the resulting SIDs are more successor-predictive, observed as a drop in the train-only prefix successor entropy and, finally, as Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 in the single frozen run. If instead the encoder drives the achievable SID set to a relabelling of the baseline's, the run lands at baseline recall and the idea is dead.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual quantizer, at every level: the base point of the composition (z_0 = p_i), the residual extraction (r_l = log_{z_{l-1}}(x_i)) and the code comparison (transported code PT_{o->z_{l-1}}(c_{l,k}) instead of the raw code). It acts during Stage 2 training of the RQ-VAE, not in Stage 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed-curvature (c=1) Lorentz operations: exponential and logarithm maps at a data-defined base point, and parallel transport PT_{x->y}(v) = v + (<y,v>_L/(1 - <x,y>_L))(x + y), all evaluated on the hyperboloid (the chart that stays numerically sound where the Poincaré chart saturates); the residual comparison uses the transported tangent vectors.
ideas.key_change: The RQ target point is the item's content point, but the composition starts at a behaviour pole p_i = exp_o(1 * u_hat_i) instead of the origin, and every codebook vector is parallel-transported from T_o into T_{z_{l-1}} before it is compared with the residual; the encoder output is projected orthogonal to u_hat_i so the encoder cannot undo the behaviour shift.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The pole table is built once, before Stage 2 starts, from the training split interactions only; validation and test interactions are never read, no Stage 3 history or Stage 3 model output is consulted, and the table is frozen (a plain buffer, no gradient, no online update) so nothing from an evaluation pass can flow back into SID construction. The t_j and t_pop used are the same frozen content embeddings the baseline RQ-VAE already consumes, so no new external signal enters.
ideas.motivation: Content-only RQ-VAE SIDs group items by what they are, but a generative next-item recommender needs prefixes that already carry "what tends to follow this" information; the repository measurements show the predictor of Recall is a behaviour CONTRAST quantity, not hierarchy and not curvature magnitude, so the contrast has to enter the code assignment itself rather than decorate it. An item whose successor contrast points one way and an item whose successor contrast points another way should not receive the same level-1 token just because their text embeddings are close.
ideas.novelty: Earlier mechanisms here changed the curvature per prefix level, ranked each item's radius by behaviour entropy, or replaced the codebook update with a curved Fréchet mean. This one keeps the curvature fixed at c=1 (the gauge is not estimated), keeps a single constant pole radius for every item (no behaviour statistic ranks items radially), and instead uses the behaviour contrast to choose the DIRECTION of a Lorentz frame change: the quantizer's residual is taken at a behaviour-defined base point and each code is parallel-transported into that base point's tangent space, so the item-specific gyration (a pure curvature effect with no Euclidean analogue at the same cost) is what mixes behaviour into the code indices.
ideas.observables: (1) level-1 code histogram and the fraction of items whose level-1 token differs from the Euclidean-shift variant evaluated once at initialisation (static, no training arm); (2) mean gyration angle of PT_{o->p_i} on the orthogonal complement, recorded at init; (3) per-epoch mean hyperbolic displacement ||log_{p_i}(x_i)|| and ||<a_i,u_hat_i>||, which must stay near zero; (4) train-only prefix behaviour predictability: mean top-1 successor hit rate of a prefix bucket versus a popularity baseline, and prefix conditional successor entropy; (5) SID collisions and distinct-SID count; (6) Stage 3 test_recall@10, the only judgement.
risks: The encoder still has second-order freedom to compensate the frame shift, so the coupling can be partially absorbed (diagnostic: record ||<a_i,u_hat_i>|| and the mean hyperbolic displacement ||log_{p_i}(x_i)|| per epoch). Items with noisy one-transition successor sets get a full-strength direction because the radius is constant, which may inject PMI noise into level-1 codes (no shrinkage by design, to stay out of the radial-ranking slot). The displacement target has norm up to 2 at radius 1, so the L-level budget is stretched and reconstruction can degrade, which would make SIDs less informative for Stage 3 even if they are more behaviour-aligned. Fixed-radius poles for rare items may also increase SID collisions where successor contrast is uninformative; collision count and distinct-SID count are recorded but are not gates.
ideas.safeguards: clamp the arcosh argument to max(1 + 1e-7, -<z,x>_L); clamp the ||u_i|| division at 1e-8 and route zero-norm poles to the origin frame; hard-clip the encoder tangent to ||a_i||<=1 (one curvature unit, matching the pole radius, so the Poincaré radius stays at or below tanh(1)=0.762, well below the c~2 saturation the repository measured) after projecting orthogonal to u_hat_i (project, then clip, then re-project once); compute every map in the Lorentz chart and convert to Poincaré only for logging; clamp the transport denominator 1 - <x,y>_L to at least 1e-6 by bounding the geodesic step at 2 curvature units (the maximum displacement reachable at this radius); renormalise z_l to <z,z>_L = -1 after each composition to stop float drift; skip the behaviour term (identity frame) for items with no train successor so no pseudo-direction is invented; no constant is fitted: c=1 is the gauge, the pole radius is one curvature unit, the PMI clip is the analytic maximum log N, the tangent bound equals the pole radius, and beta is inherited from the baseline recipe.
ideas.spec_equations: exp^c_o(v) = cosh(||v||)*o + sinh(||v||)/||v||*v in (time, space) coordinates with ||v|| the Euclidean tangent norm and c=1; log^c_o(x) = arcosh(-<x,o>_L) * (x + <x,o>_L o)/||x + <x,o>_L o||; log^c_z(x) = d * (x + <z,x>_L z)/||x + <z,x>_L z|| with d = arcosh(-<z,x>_L); PT^c_{x->y}(v) = v + (<y,v>_L/(1 - <x,y>_L))(x + y); composition z_l = exp_{z_{l-1}}(PT_{o->z_{l-1}}(c_{l,k_l})); assignment k_l = argmin_k ||log_{z_{l-1}}(x_i) - PT_{o->z_{l-1}}(c_{l,k})||^2; losses L_rec = sum_l ||r_l - c~_{l,k_l}||^2, L_cb = sum_l ||r_l - sg(c~)||^2, L_cm = beta sum_l ||sg(r_l) - c~||^2 with beta the baseline commitment weight unchanged, plus the baseline content reconstruction and decoder terms; SID = (k_1..k_L); pole u_i = sum_j A_ij t_j - (sum_j A_ij) t_pop, A_ij = min(log N, max(0, log(N n_ij/(n_i n_j)))), u_hat_i = u_i/max(||u_i||, 1e-8), p_i = exp_o(u_hat_i) if ||u_i|| > 1e-8 else p_i = o; a_i <- (a_i - <a_i,u_hat_i> u_hat_i) * min(1, 1/||a_i - <a_i,u_hat_i> u_hat_i||).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: item id, its frozen content embedding e_i, the frozen pole row u_hat_i (or zero), the L codebooks c_{l,k} in T_o, the baseline commitment weight beta. Outputs: the L-tuple SID, the reconstructed tangent d_i = log_o(z_L) for the decoder, and the three RQ losses; the codebooks receive gradients through the transported codes and through the moving-frame residuals.

specification.text: Lorentz model, curvature c=1 fixed, signature (-,+,...,+), <x,x>_L = -1. Pole: u_i = sum_{j in succ(i)} A_ij t_j - (sum_j A_ij) t_pop, A_ij = max(0, log(N*n_ij/(n_i*n_j))) clipped at log N, t_pop = popularity-weighted mean text direction; u_hat_i = u_i/||u_i||, p_i = exp_o(u_hat_i) (geodesic radius exactly 1, Poincaré radius tanh(1)=0.762, below the measured saturation point). Encoder: a_i = f_phi(e_i) projected orthogonal to u_hat_i and clipped to ||a_i||<=1. Item point x_i = exp_o(a_i). Quantization: z_0 = p_i; for l=1..L, r_l = log_{z_{l-1}}(x_i), k_l = argmin_k || r_l - PT_{o->z_{l-1}}(c_{l,k}) ||^2, z_l = exp_{z_{l-1}}( PT_{o->z_{l-1}}(c_{l,k_l}) ). SID(i) = (k_1,...,k_L). The decoder keeps the baseline content reconstruction from d_i = log_o(z_L). Loss = baseline reconstruction + sum_l [ ||r_l - c~_{l,k_l}||^2 + ||r_l - sg(c~)||^2 + beta ||sg(r_l) - c~||^2 ] with c~ = PT_{o->z_{l-1}}(c_{l,k}).

ideas.title: Behaviour-pole gyroframe residual quantization: RQ codes are emitted, assigned and composed inside the moving Lorentz frame of each item's train-only successor-contrast direction, with the pole at a constant one-curvature-unit radius.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: alpha_i forced to 0 for every item and s_i forced to 0 (so u_i = 0), leaving exp/log/PT/d_H exactly as specified; the anchor collapses to q_l and the run is a pure Lorentz residual chain. Not trained in this round, but wired and unit-checked to reproduce baseline residuals bit-for-bit within tolerance.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full coupled mechanism exactly as specified - alpha_i from train-only transition asymmetry, delta_i = alpha_i * d_H(O,q_l), Lorentz log/exp/PT and Lorentz nearest-codeword scoring. This is the single arm that is trained and the only arm judged.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: every exp/log/PT replaced by its linear/Euclidean counterpart (q~ = q + delta_i * v_i with delta_i = alpha_i * ||q_l||, r = z - q~, assignment by L2), behaviour left on; the same alpha_i and s_i enter a flat residual chain. Not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only: scan each training session, insert directed edges (item at position t -> item at position t+1) into a sparse counter to obtain n_ij; normalise rows to p_i and columns to p~_i; alpha_i = 0.5 * L1 distance between the two distributions; s_i = sum_j p_i(j) e_j with e_j the frozen side embedding already fed to the RQ-VAE. Everything is recomputed once before Stage 2 and cached; items with no in- or out-edges get alpha_i = 0, s_i = 0 and reduce exactly to the baseline.
ideas.behavior_signal: Per-item forward/backward transition asymmetry of the sequential training graph, alpha_i in [0,1], together with the successor-averaged side-embedding direction s_i.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-time pass over training sessions to build sparse n_ij and s_i (O(#train transitions), minutes, CPU, cached). Per step nothing changes in the transformer; the added work is 4096 items x 3 levels x (one log, one exp, two parallel transports, ~4 d-dimensional ops) plus a 4096 x 3 x 257 Lorentz-dot assignment in R^(d+1), about 1.1e8 FLOPs forward per step against a transformer step of order 1e12, i.e. well under 1% per step. Per epoch at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps, 3000 epochs) the re-anchoring is ~1.2e9 FLOPs per epoch, no extra codebook entries and one extra d_in x d matrix; measured wall-clock expectation +1% to +2% on the four-card Stage 2 run, negligible on Stage 3 because Stage 3 consumes the emitted SIDs only.
ideas.coupling_equation: q~_{i,l} = exp_{q_l}( alpha_i * d_H(O, q_l) * u_{i,l} ), r_{i,l} = PT_{q~_{i,l} -> O}( log_{q~_{i,l}}( z_{i,l} ) ), a_{i,l+1} = argmin_k d_H( exp_O(r_{i,l}), q_{l+1,k} ), where alpha_i is the behaviour term and d_H/exp/log/PT are the curved terms.
ideas.coupling_path: The behaviour term and the curved term produce the same object: q~_l = exp_{q_l}( alpha_i * d_H(O,q_l) * PT_{O->q_l}(P s_i / ||P s_i||) ). That object is simultaneously the anchor whose log map defines the residual handed to level l+1 and the point against which level l+1's Lorentz assignment is effectively scored, so setting alpha_i = 0 removes the behaviour and reverting exp/PT/d_H to their Euclidean forms removes the curve; either change alters the residual vector and therefore the SID token produced at level l+1.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the radial coordinate is the uninformative part of the code space (evidence 3) and behaviour contrast is the informative part, then removing radius from the residual should make levels 2 and 3 encode behaviour-distinguishing direction, so the train-split conditional entropy H(next | 2-level prefix) and H(next | 3-level prefix) at fixed first token should fall relative to the frozen baseline, level-2/3 code usage should spread rather than concentrate on a few radial codes, and Stage 3 test_recall@10 should exceed 0.065 in the single frozen run. If the residual re-anchoring is neutral (delta too small to matter because most codewords sit near the origin) the diagnostics will show unchanged level-2 entropy and unchanged recall, which is the falsification.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer, at every level l >= 1, in the forward assignment path - the anchor of the log map, the transport of the residual, and the nearest-codeword scoring. It does not act on the loss scaling, on Stage 3, or on any standalone regulariser.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Curvature -1 fixed by the documented gauge on the Lorentz hyperboloid: exponential map exp_x(v) = cosh(||v||) x + sinh(||v||) v/||v||, logarithmic map log_x(y) = arcosh(alpha)/sqrt(alpha^2-1) * (y - alpha x) with alpha = -<x,y>_L, parallel transport PT_{x->y}(v) = v + (<y,v>_L / (1 - <x,y>_L)) (x + y), and geodesic distance d_H = arcosh(-<x,y>_L). No trainable curvature: it is a gauge, and the mechanism does not claim to identify it.
ideas.key_change: At every RQ level the residual is taken at a displaced anchor q~ = exp_q(delta_i * u_i) instead of at the codeword q, where delta_i is the item's train-only forward/backward transition asymmetry times the codeword's own hyperbolic radius and u_i is the parallel transport to q of the successor-centroid direction; the next-level input is the parallel transport of log_{q~}(z) back to the origin and every assignment uses the Lorentz distance.
ideas.leakage_boundary: n_ij, alpha_i and s_i are built exclusively from the sequential training interactions, the same split that trains the RQ-VAE and Stage 3; validation and test sessions are never read by the statistics pass, so no validation or test interaction can enter the SID construction. The side embeddings e_j are the model's frozen item features, not interaction-derived, so they carry no split leakage. The statistics are constants w.r.t. the Stage 2 graph, so no validation signal can be laundered through them.
ideas.motivation: Evidence in this repository says the useful SID metric family is behaviour *contrast*, and that its Euclidean control matches the hyperbolic form, while the radial coordinate is only group compactness and the four-point/tree premise is unavailable. That leaves one unexamined place for geometry to do real work: the quantization residual. In a Euclidean RQ chain the residual z - q mixes radial error (which the evidence says is uninformative) with directional error (which carries behaviour identity), so levels 2 and 3 spend their codebook capacity re-encoding radius. BCGR makes the residual an angular, behaviour-oriented quantity: it measures the correction from a point displaced along the item's train-only behavioural flow, in a chart where pure radius changes are cheap and direction changes are expensive.
ideas.novelty: Prior mechanisms here changed the codebook update rule (successor-weighted Frechet means), the per-level curvature (CURVCTRL), or the item radius (BRad). BCGR changes none of those: the codebook, the number of levels and the loss terms are untouched. It changes *where the log map is taken from* - the residual anchor is displaced by a behaviour-contrast term - and it therefore changes what levels >= 2 are asked to encode (behaviour-orthogonal direction instead of radius). No cone, no prefix-transition score, no Gromov-delta weight, no radial ranking.
ideas.observables: (i) SID assignment: level-2 and level-3 code usage entropy and the number of distinct level-2 codes used per level-1 prefix should increase; the fraction of items whose full SID changes relative to a stored baseline SID table should be substantial (recorded, not gated). (ii) Prefix behaviour predictability on the training split: H(next | 2-token prefix) and H(next | 3-token prefix) at fixed first token should decrease. (iii) Behaviour contrast diagnostics (HBAA contrast, adjacency, transfer predictability) recorded, never used as a gate. (iv) Stage 3 test_recall@10 from the single frozen Stage 3 run.
risks: (1) Early in training P and the codebook are unaligned, so u_i points somewhere unhelpful and the displacement injects noise into levels 2-3; 3000 epochs may not be enough to recover. (2) If codewords cluster near the origin, d_H(O,q) ~ 0 and delta ~ 0, making the mechanism a no-op - this is detectable in the diagnostics but leaves the run uninformative. (3) Behaviour contrast may already be fully exploited by the level-1 assignment, so the residual change is redundant. (4) The learned P has a single gradient pathway and could collapse to a constant direction, in which case alpha only rescales a fixed displacement (harmless but weak).
ideas.safeguards: (1) clamp the arcosh argument to >= 1 + 1e-7 and the Lorentz inner product to <= -1 - 1e-7 before the distance; (2) clamp every point back onto the hyperboloid after exp (renormalise so <x,x>_L = -1) to stop float drift off the manifold; (3) guard ||v|| and ||log|| with 1e-8 floors and use the series limit for alpha near 1; (4) cap delta at 0.5 * d_H(O,q) so the anchor can never cross the origin or leave the region where the log map is well conditioned; (5) clamp the transported residual norm to the 99.9th percentile of the batch per level (a measured, per-batch quantile, not a tuned constant) so a single outlier cannot dominate the commitment term; (6) items with alpha_i = 0 take the exact baseline branch, so no degenerate direction can enter; (7) keep the Lorentz chart throughout (the Poincare chart saturates above c ~ 2 and is never used); (8) fix the gauge at c = 1 and apply any curvature change only as the sqrt(c) rescaling, never as a fitted parameter.
ideas.spec_equations:
precompute (CPU, once): n_ij from train sessions; p_i(j) = n_ij / sum_j n_ij; p~_i(j) = n_ji / sum_j n_ji; alpha_i = 0.5 * sum_j |p_i(j) - p~_i(j)|; s_i = sum_j p_i(j) e_j. Init P ~ N(0, 1/d_in).
forward(item i, latent z): x_1 = L(z); for l in 1..L: q = q_l[a_l]; if alpha_i == 0 or ||s_i|| == 0: r = PT_{q->O}(log_q(x_l)) else: v = P s_i; v = v / max(||v||, 1e-8); u = PT_{O->q}(v); delta = min(alpha_i * d_H(O,q), 0.5 * d_H(O,q)); qt = exp_q(delta * u); r = PT_{qt->O}(log_{qt}(x_l)); x_{l+1} = exp_O(r); logits_k = -d_H(x_{l+1}, q_{l+1,k}); a_{l+1} = argmax_k logits_k; store r for the commitment term. Return the token tuple (a_1..a_L). Loss = baseline reconstruction + ||r_l||^2 (straight-through on x_{l+1} as in the frozen recipe).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: the frozen side embeddings e_j (R^{d_in}), the sparse train transition counts, the current batch latents z (R^d), the per-level Lorentz codebooks Q_l (R^{(d+1) x K}), the linear map P. Outputs: per item a discrete SID token tuple and the per-level residual tangents r_l used by the commitment term; a cached alpha_i, s_i table is emitted to disk for audit.

specification.text:
Fix the gauge at curvature c = 1 (documented choice; re-scaling by sqrt(c) reproduces any other curvature exactly). Work on the hyperboloid H^d = {x in R^{d+1}: <x,x>_L = -1}, <u,v>_L = -u0 v0 + u.v, lift L(z) = (sqrt(1+||z||^2), z), d_H(x,y) = arcosh(clamp(-<x,y>_L, 1+1e-7, inf)).
Train-only statistics per item i: n_ij = number of times item j directly follows item i in training sessions; p_i(j) = n_ij / sum_j n_ij, p~_i(j) = n_ji / sum_j n_ji; alpha_i = 0.5 * sum_j |p_i(j) - p~_i(j)| in [0,1]; s_i = sum_j p_i(j) * e_j with e_j the frozen side/text embedding of item j; v_i = P s_i / max(||P s_i||, 1e-8) with P a learned d_in x d linear map; u_i = PT_{O->q}(v_i) with O = (1,0,...,0).
Per level l with codeword q_l: delta_i = alpha_i * d_H(O, q_l) (automatically <= d_H(O,q_l), clipped at 0.5 * d_H(O,q_l) for safety); q~_l = exp_{q_l}(delta_i * u_i); residual tangent r_l = PT_{q~_l -> O}( log_{q~_l}( L(z_l) ) ); next input z_{l+1} = exp_O(r_l); assignment a_{l+1} = argmin_k d_H(L(z_{l+1}), q_{l+1,k}). Commitment term uses ||r_l||^2 in place of ||z_l - q_l||^2; reconstruction loss unchanged. alpha_i = 0 -> delta = 0 -> exact baseline anchor.

ideas.title: Behaviour-contrast geodesic re-anchoring of the RQ-VAE residual chain in the Lorentz model

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: m_i := 0 for all i (the u table and anchor buffer zeroed), so the recursion becomes p_{l+1} = (-q_{k_l}) (+) p_l, i.e. pure hyperbolic RQ with no behaviour frame. Wired as a config flag; not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The trained arm: c = 1 with the Mobius recursion and m_i = tanh(rho) u_i active. This is the single formal run (3000 Stage 2 epochs, four-GPU DDP, batch 4096, frozen recipe) followed by the frozen Stage 3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c := 0 path, where (+) becomes +, E_sigma and L_sigma become identity and d_P becomes squared Euclidean, so the recursion becomes r_{l+1} = r_l - e_{k_l} - m_i, i.e. behaviour enters only as a constant per-item offset. Same flag structure; not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the sequential TRAINING interactions only, unit edges, no truncation, using the same builder as the evidence graph: A_ij = number of training-split transitions i -> j; o_i = sum_j A_ij; iota_j = sum_i A_ij; T = sum_ij A_ij. Contrast weight w_ij = max(0, ln(A_ij * T / (o_i * iota_j))) for A_ij >= 1, else 0. With x_i^txt the frozen Stage 2 item text embedding, c_i = sum_j w_ij (x_j^txt - x_i^txt) and u_i = c_i / ||c_i|| (u_i = 0 when o_i = 0 or ||c_i|| < 1e-12). The tables {u_i} and {m_i} are computed once before the run and frozen.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directional positive-PMI transition contrast per item (popularity-adjusted directed transitions), not a co-occurrence count and not a hierarchy statistic.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute once, offline, before training: the sparse train-transition PMI weights plus one sparse-times-dense product (~10^6 edges x 768 dims ~ 0.8 GFLOP), and the 24556 x 768 anchor table (75 MB float32); a few seconds to one minute, zero per-step cost afterwards. Per training step (global batch 4096, L levels, d = 768): L x 4096 x 768 x ~10 flops ~ 1.3e8 FLOPs = 0.13 GFLOP plus ~4 extra 4096 x 768 activations (~55 MB); that is under 1-2% of a transformer step. At the frozen scale 24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps, total extra ~9.4 TFLOP, wall-clock overhead about 1%. No new trainable parameters; the anchor table is a non-trainable buffer.
ideas.coupling_equation: p_{l+1} = (-E_sigma(e_{k_l})) (+)_c ( (-m_i) (+)_c E_sigma(r_l) ), with k_l = argmin_k d_P^c(E_sigma(r_l), E_sigma(e_k)) and m_i = tanh(rho) * u_i from the positive-PMI behaviour contrast direction; equivalently r_{l+1} = L_sigma(p_{l+1}).
ideas.coupling_path: u_i (behaviour) -> m_i = tanh(rho) u_i (a point in the ball) -> Mobius gyro-translation of the level-l residual point -> curved subtraction of the chosen code -> r_{l+1} -> level-(l+1) assignment. Setting m_i = 0 collapses the translation to the identity and changes every level>=2 code; setting c = 0 turns the translation into a plain offset and changes the codes. Neither factor can be deleted without changing which codes are chosen, so they are one pathway rather than two losses.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: For the idea to be worth keeping, the behaviour frame must move deep-level capacity away from global position and toward transition-relevant deviation, so that a 3-token prefix becomes more predictive of the training successor set and the frozen Stage3 beam puts the true item in the top 10 more often than 0.065. Observable: at the final checkpoint, evaluating the same weights with m_i forced to 0 (forward pass only, no retraining) must change a large fraction of level>=2 codes and worsen the train-split prefix successor rank; if the both-on run's Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 while the geometry-off switch on the same checkpoint yields different level>=2 codes, the coupling is doing work.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual quantizer recursion at every level l >= 1 of RQ-VAE training: in the assignment cost and in the residual update that feeds level l+1, and in the codebook commitment through the curved residual.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 (unit Poincare ball), used through three explicit curved operations: exp_0 / log_0 at a frozen tangent scale sigma (tanh and artanh), the Mobius addition (+)_c with its inverse (-x)(+)_c y, and the Poincare distance d_P(x,y) = acosh(1 + 2c||x-y||^2 / ((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2)))/sqrt(c). Curvature is never estimated or tuned; c=1 is a documented gauge choice consistent with the repo finding that c only rescales tangent vectors.
ideas.key_change: At each level the residual point is moved into the item's behaviour frame by the Poincare isometry tau_{m_i}, the chosen code is subtracted there by Mobius addition, and the result is logged back to the tangent space to become the next residual, so the codes chosen at levels 2..L are determined jointly by the behaviour direction and by the curved frame change.
ideas.leakage_boundary: A is built from training-split sequences only; validation and test interactions never enter A, w, u, m, rho or sigma. rho is measured from the first training forward pass and sigma from the training text embeddings. No validation or test statistic selects any constant, so the SID construction is a pure function of (training transitions, training text embeddings, frozen constants) and nothing from the evaluation splits can reach the codebook or the tokens.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are built by subtracting codebook vectors from a residual, so every deeper level re-encodes the item's absolute position rather than what distinguishes it from the items it is actually confused with at recommendation time. The repository evidence shows that what predicts Stage3 recall is behaviour contrast (HBAA +0.7104) and not hierarchy, curvature estimation or radial compactness, yet the quantizer recursion has no notion of where an item's behaviour is heading; its levels 2..L are spent on global geometry instead of behaviour-relevant deviation.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds changed the codebook (Poincare-Frechet successor centroids), the per-level curvature (CURVCTRL-SID), the radial slot (BRad-RQ), the prefix cone (behcone-prefix-rq), successor profile smoothing (LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ), successor boosting (succboost-geoshift), MoE branching (BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ) and multi-curvature fibres (MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ). None of them touches the residual recursion operator itself. GYROFRAME-RQ changes p_{l+1} from "p_l minus code" to "p_l minus code, re-expressed in a per-item frame that is gyro-translated by the item's behaviour contrast direction". The displacement is directional only (constant hyperbolic radius), so it is not a radial or depth ranking, and curvature is never estimated (fixed c=1, explicitly a gauge choice).
ideas.observables: (1) SID assignment: per-level code usage histograms and the fraction of items whose level>=2 tokens differ between the trained weights evaluated with m_i and with m_i = 0 (one forward pass each, no retraining). (2) Per-level mean tangent norm ||r_l||, which should stop growing with l if the frame absorbs position. (3) Train-split prefix successor predictability: mean rank and hit rate of the true successor given the level-l prefix, for l = 1..L. (4) Frozen Stage3 test_recall@10, the only judgement.
risks: The frame offset may be noise for items whose PMI direction is dominated by popularity artefacts (reduced but not removed by the PMI normalisation). The discrete argmin passes gradient to the curved chain only through the straight-through cost, so the codebook may adapt weakly and the frame may act as a fixed perturbation. If latents crowd the ball boundary, artanh saturation makes the frame change enormous. The constant-radius anchor may be too weak or may dominate. Stage3 may simply ignore the changed tokens, in which case one run cannot tell which sub-part failed.
ideas.safeguards: (a) clamp every ball point to norm <= 1-1e-5 before Mobius addition and before acosh; (b) clamp the acosh argument to >= 1+1e-7 and (1-||x||^2) to >= 1e-5; (c) use artanh(t) = 0.5*log((1+t)/(1-t)) with t clamped to 1-1e-6 and a zero-norm guard returning 0; (d) floor the Mobius denominator at 1e-8 and fall back to the Euclidean update on the affected rows, counting and logging them; (e) u_i = 0 for o_i = 0 or ||c_i|| < 1e-12, so out-degree-zero items keep m_i = 0; (f) PMI defined only on A_ij >= 1, so no log(0); (g) float32 forward with a float64 Mobius-identity check on 16 random rows once per epoch; (h) curvature is a compile-time constant c = 1, so no curvature drift; (i) sigma and rho are frozen after epoch 0 so the frame cannot co-adapt into a scale search.
ideas.spec_equations: Constants fixed before the run: c = 1; sigma = 1/R with R = the 95th percentile of ||z_i|| over training items at the end of epoch 0 (measured, then frozen); rho = median_i ||r_{i,1}|| over training items at the end of epoch 0 (measured, then frozen). Ball maps: E_sigma(r) = tanh(sigma||r||)/(sigma||r||) * r; L_sigma(p) = artanh(||p||)/(sigma||p||) * p, with ||p|| clamped to 1-1e-5, and E_sigma(0) = L_sigma(0) = 0. Mobius (c = 1): x (+) y = ((1 + 2<x,y> + ||y||^2) x + (1 - ||x||^2) y) / (1 + 2<x,y> + ||x||^2 ||y||^2). Forward for item i with encoder latent z_i: r_1 = z_i; for l = 1..L: p_l = E_sigma(r_l); q_k = E_sigma(e_k); cost_l(k) = acosh(1 + 2||p_l - q_k||^2 / ((1-||p_l||^2)(1-||q_k||^2))); k_l = argmin_k cost_l(k); code contribution e_{k_l} taken straight-through; p_next = (-q_{k_l}) (+) ((-m_i) (+) p_l); r_{l+1} = L_sigma(p_next). SID_i = (k_1,...,k_L). Reconstruction x_hat_i = Dec(sum_l e_{k_l}); loss = ||x_hat_i - x_i^txt||^2 + beta||z_i - sg(sum_l e_{k_l})||^2 + lambda_cb||sum_l e_{k_l} - sg(z_i)||^2 with the frozen baseline beta and lambda_cb unchanged. Offline: A, w, u, m exactly as in BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are the training-split transition matrix A (sparse, N x N), the frozen item text embeddings X in R^{N x d}, the encoder latent z_i, and the codebook E in R^{K x d}. Outputs are the precomputed anchor table m in R^{N x d}, the per-level code indices (k_1..k_L) per item, the curved residual chain r_1..r_{L+1} used for assignment and for the commitment term, and gradients to the encoder, codebook and decoder.

specification.text: k_l = argmin_k d_P(E_sigma(r_l), E_sigma(e_k)); p_{l+1} = (-E_sigma(e_{k_l})) (+) ((-m_i) (+) E_sigma(r_l)); r_{l+1} = L_sigma(p_{l+1}); m_i = tanh(rho) u_i, where u_i is the positive-PMI transition contrast direction and rho, sigma are measured once and frozen. Full equations under SPEC EQUATIONS.

ideas.title: Behaviour-conditioned moving frame (Mobius gyro-translation by a positive-PMI transition direction) for the RQ-VAE residual recursion in a fixed-curvature Poincare ball

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: b_i := 0 for all items, so g_i = 1 and g_{l,k} = 1; the same Lorentz distance and the same tau are used and everything else is identical.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full coupled run, g = exp(b/4) multiplying the c = 1 Lorentz arccosh distance; the only arm trained.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: d_Lorentz replaced by the Euclidean tangent distance ||t_i^l - e_{l,k}||_2 inside the same product, with tau_l = mean_k ||e_{l,k}||^2 unchanged; b and g unchanged.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only: iterate each user's sessions in timestamp order, add unit edge i->j for consecutive items, accumulate C_ij; d_i = sum_j C_ij; P_ij = C_ij/d_i; q_i = sum_j P_ij^2; u_i = log(q_i d_i); b_i = clip(z-score(u), -2, 2), frozen before training. No validation or test interactions are ever read.
ideas.behavior_signal: Degree-corrected successor concentration b_i of each training item, from directed item-to-item transitions in the Stage-2 training interactions.
ideas.cost_estimate: One extra O(N_items * L * K) pass per epoch for the responsibility-weighted g (24556 * 3 * 256 = 18.9M adds), plus an arccosh and a Lorentz dot replacing the squared Euclidean per pair: about 18.9M arccosh per epoch, i.e. 786k per step over 24 steps, well under 1% of a transformer step at global batch 4096; no extra parameters beyond the frozen 24556-float b vector; roughly +2-4% wall clock on Stage 2, unchanged Stage 3.
ideas.coupling_equation: s_ik = - ( g_{l,k}(b) * arccosh(-<exp_0(t_i^l), exp_0(e_{l,k})>_L) )^2 / tau_l , with g_{l,k}(b) = sum_i w_ik exp(b_i/4) / sum_i w_ik.
ideas.coupling_path: b_i -> g_i -> g_{l,k} -> distance g_{l,k} * d_Lorentz(x_i, y_{l,k}) -> assignment logits -> hard code index -> level-l SID digit -> prefix -> Stage-3 recall. Removing behaviour sets b_i = 0 hence g = 1 and the distance is the plain Lorentz distance; removing geometry replaces d_Lorentz by the Euclidean tangent distance and the product becomes a behaviour-weighted Euclidean distance. Either removal changes the core assignment computation, not a side loss.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the conformal stretch aligns code resolution with successor concentration, then the behaviour-weighted level-1 and level-2 quantization error should fall for high-b items at unchanged code usage, prefix transition entropy should drop for the high-b item subset, and Stage 3 test_recall@10 should exceed 0.065. It is worth keeping if that recall is above 0.065 and the behaviour-weighted quantization error falls; it is not worth keeping if g_{l,k} is nearly constant (signal washed out) or if high-b and low-b item recall move together with no prefix change.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE residual assignment at every quantization level, i.e. the code-entry selection step that produces each SID digit; the codebook update rule and the decoder are unchanged.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz (hyperboloid) geodesic distance d_L(x,y) = arccosh(-<x,y>_L) at fixed curvature c = 1, multiplied by a conformal factor g; tangent lift x = (sqrt(1+||t||^2), t) is the exp map at the origin.
ideas.key_change: Compute a per-item degree-corrected successor-concentration score b_i from train-only directed transitions; map it to a per-code conformal weight g_{l,k} (stop-gradient responsibility-weighted mean of g_i = exp(b_i/4)); use g_{l,k} * d_Lorentz(x_i^l, y_{l,k}) as the assignment distance at every RQ level instead of the plain distance, with the codebook update unchanged.
ideas.leakage_boundary: C_ij, d_i, and the mean/std of u are computed at preprocessing time from the training interaction file only, written to a read-only 24556-vector, and never recomputed during validation or test; Stage 3 consumes only integer SIDs produced in Stage 2, so no validation or test user-item pair can influence b_i, g_{l,k}, or the codebook.
ideas.motivation: The evidence says SID quality is predicted by behaviour contrast, not by hierarchy: HBAA-style distance contrast tracks recall (+0.71) while Gromov-delta and ancestor-depth weighting hurt. Degree-matched rewiring is as tree-like as the real graph, so "the data is a tree" is unavailable. What is still unused is the graph's own local concentration: some items have highly predictable next items (successor mass concentrated on few neighbours), others disperse it. A quantizer that spends its finite code resolution uniformly ignores exactly that contrast. This idea makes the behaviour contrast enter the metric tensor of the code space, so the quantizer resolves predictable regions more finely and dispersive regions more coarsely, which is where prefix transfer is already easy.
ideas.novelty: Earlier attempts either weighted the assignment/outer product by transitions (Sinkhorn or behaviour-weighted assignment), set per-level or per-prefix curvature from transition statistics (CURVCTRL-SID, BRad-RQ put it in the radial coordinate, SUCC-GEO-CBTAB and Poincare-Frechet put it in the update rule). None changes the METRIC ITSELF as a function of the item's successor concentration: here the behaviour scalar is a conformal factor multiplying a fixed-curvature Lorentz distance, so the behaviour term appears inside the distance and the distance carries curvature in one expression. Curvature is held at c=1 and never estimated, respecting the gauge result (any estimated c is a radial rescale). No Frechet/Karcher codebook update, no curvature prediction from prefixes, no radial term.
ideas.observables: per-level code usage histogram and perplexity; g_{l,k} distribution (must stay non-degenerate); behaviour-weighted quantization error split by b_i tercile; level-1 and level-2 prefix transition entropy on the training split; SID collision count; Stage 3 test_recall@10.
risks: b_i may mostly encode popularity (mitigated by the degree-matched null, not guaranteed); the conformal factor may act as noise and shift code assignment without changing prefix predictability; soft responsibility may be dominated by a few hub codes so g_{l,k} collapses to 1; if high-b items are already saturated in Stage 3 the recall gain is nil; arccosh gradients blow up near the light cone if the clamp is wrong.
ideas.safeguards: clamp the arccosh argument at 1+1e-7 (double precision for the inner product, then cast); radial clamp ||t|| <= tanh^{-1}(0.99) and ||e|| likewise so the lift never reaches the light cone; tau_l floored at 1e-6 to avoid division by zero when a level collapses; g_i predefined in [0.607, 1.649] and g_{l,k} additionally clipped to the same interval; codes with sum_i w_ik < 2 inherit g_{l,k} = 1 (no behaviour estimate); stop-gradient on g_{l,k} so the behaviour term cannot be gamed by the encoder; items with d_i < 2 get b_i = 0; if the code usage perplexity of a level falls below 1.2 the run is reported as collapsed (diagnostic, not a gate).
ideas.spec_equations:
u_i = log( (sum_j (C_ij/d_i)^2) * d_i ),  b_i = clip((u_i - mu_u)/sigma_u, -2, 2),  g_i = exp(b_i/4)
x_i^l = ( sqrt(1+||t_i^l||^2), t_i^l ),  y_{l,k} = ( sqrt(1+||e_{l,k}||^2), e_{l,k} )
<s,t>_L = -s_0 t_0 + s_1 t_1 + ... + s_d t_d
d_L = arccosh( clamp(-<x,y>_L, 1+1e-7, +inf) )
s_ik = - ( g_{l,k} * d_L )^2 / tau_l,  p_ik = softmax_k(s_ik)
k_i^l = argmax_k p_ik (straight-through),  SID(i) = (k_i^1, k_i^2, k_i^3)
g_{l,k} = sum_i w_ik g_i / (sum_i w_ik + 1e-8),  w_ik = 1[k_i^l = k], stop-gradient

ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: train-only transition counts C (24556 x 24556 sparse, ~1e7 edges), frozen b (24556,), per-level codebooks e_{l,k} (L x 256 x d), residual tangents t_i^l (batch x d). Outputs: g_{l,k} (L x 256), assignment logits s (batch x 256 per level), hard codes and hence SID tuples, plus the diagnostic tensors above.

specification.text:
1. Train-only transitions: from the Stage-2 training split only, for each user session in timestamp order add a unit edge i -> j between consecutive distinct items; accumulate C_ij. d_i = sum_j C_ij, P_ij = C_ij / d_i.
2. Behaviour scalar: q_i = sum_j P_ij^2 (successor concentration). Degree-matched null q_i^0 = 1/d_i. u_i = log(q_i * d_i) for d_i >= 2, else u_i = 0. b_i = clip((u_i - mean(u)) / std(u), -2, +2) over the 24556 training items (mean/std computed once on the training split, frozen).
3. Conformal weight: g_i = exp(b_i / 4) in [e^-0.5, e^+0.5] = [0.607, 1.649].
4. Hyperbolic lift (fixed c = 1, Lorentz chart): for tangent vector t, x = (sqrt(1+||t||^2), t), with radial clamp ||t|| <= tanh^{-1}(0.99).
5. Code lift: y_{l,k} = (sqrt(1+||e_{l,k}||^2), e_{l,k}).
6. Assignment logits: s_ik = - ( g_{l,k} * arccosh(-<x_i^l, y_{l,k}>_L) )^2 / tau_l, tau_l = mean_k ||e_{l,k}||^2, softmax over k, straight-through hard code for the SID.
7. g_{l,k} = sum_i w_ik g_i / (sum_i w_ik + 1e-8), with w_ik the previous-epoch hard assignment indicator of item i to code (l,k); stop-gradient, recomputed once per epoch.
8. Decoder input is the tangent image log_0(y_{l,k}) = e_{l,k} of the selected code (unchanged from baseline), so the generative model and Stage 3 see only integer SIDs.

objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

One mechanism for this round, along the chain: user behaviour data -> behaviour graph -> verify the tree structure -> behaviour item embedding -> Gromov delta -> hyperbolic curvature -> text embedding into a hyperbolic RQ-VAE -> behaviour supervision -> SID -> Stage3 -> test_recall@10. The target is a real test_recall@10 above 0.065 from one frozen four-GPU Stage2 run and one frozen Stage3 run.

EVIDENCE THE PROPOSALS MUST RESPECT (measured in this repository, results/research/issue126 and results/research/121):
1. The interaction graph built from the sequential training interactions (unit edges, no truncation) has a tree-like shortest-path metric -- about 53% of random quadruples satisfy the four-point condition exactly -- but a degree-preserving rewiring of the same graph is EXACTLY as tree-like (identical median, mean delta 0.25257 against 0.25211 +- 0.00183 over ten seeds). The four-point condition therefore does not distinguish the behaviour structure from a degree-matched random graph, so 'the behaviour data is a tree' is NOT available as a premise.
2. The curvature parameter is a GAUGE: scaling the tangent vectors by 1/sqrt(c) reproduces curvature 1 to machine precision, so a curvature estimate is a choice of radial scale, not an identified property of the data. The Poincare chart saturates above c of order 2 and only the Lorentz chart stays numerically sound there; the two charts agree below that.
3. On the 107 confirmed SID/recall pairs the metrics that predict Recall are BEHAVIOUR CONTRAST metrics and their Euclidean controls match or beat the hyperbolic forms: HBAA plain distance contrast +0.7104, its Euclidean control +0.7170, the unweighted four-point agreement +0.6593. Gromov-delta weighting and ancestor-depth weighting both HURT (-0.12 and -0.075). The radial term is group compactness, not hierarchy (91% correlated with the within-group dispersion, 0.98 with the distance to a random point, and a full permutation of the radius values collapses the correlation to the baseline).
4. So the mechanism cannot lean on 'the data is hierarchical' or on 'curvature helps'. It has to couple a train-only behaviour signal with an explicit curve operation in ONE connected computational path, and it has to be defensible on grounds other than the tree premise: the geometry of the code space, the behaviour contrast itself, or the interaction between the quantization residual and a curved distance.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: a single formal training run (3000 epochs, four-GPU DDP, global batch 4096, frozen recipe), no ablation arms, no hyperparameter tuning, no seed sweeps; every constant must be derivable a priori. The behaviour-off / geometry-off / both-on switches must exist in the code and be wired correctly, but only the both-on arm is trained. Stage3 keeps its frozen protocol (150 epochs, eval interval 5, eval start 75, early evals 25/50/75/100/125, seed 42, beam 20, no eval, test on). Stage2->Stage3 admission is technical validity only; test_recall@10 > 0.065 is the final judgement.

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
